title: Isolation precautions

findings.where: isolation.jsx: CONDITIONS rubella entries and precautionFor()
findings.title: Congenital rubella can incorrectly select Droplet
findings.problem: precautionFor("A newborn has congenital infection caused by rubella virus.") returns droplet precautions. The congenital entry recognizes only the adjacent phrase "congenital rubella"; the generic rubella entry then defaults to acquired disease. This labels surgical-mask precautions as needed while failing to select Contact.
findings.fix: Use structured congenital/acquired status, or abstain when the form cannot be established. Recognize congenital status beyond one exact adjacent phrase. Add this input as a regression test expecting Contact or null, never Droplet.

findings.title: Later-sentence treatment status is ignored
findings.problem: precautionFor("The client has head lice. Effective treatment was completed 48 hours ago.") returns Contact and produces "Needed for this client." Treatment cues are checked only in sentences naming a recognized condition, so the second sentence is ignored. This contradicts the diagram's own 24-hour discontinuation rule. The same defect affects resolution information for other infections.
findings.fix: Resolve treatment and resolution status across the relevant client narrative before asserting current precautions. Prefer structured condition/status inputs; otherwise return null when a later sentence may change applicability. Add split-sentence regression cases.

findings.where: Images 1, 3–5, 7, 8, 10–12 and 14: Contact/Droplet Room text; steps contact and droplet
findings.title: The displayed cohorting rule drops the compatibility requirement
findings.problem: Fact 2 requires compatible additional precautions, but the picture and narration reduce eligibility to having the same pathogen. "Clients with the same pathogen can share" is too permissive: an influenza-only client should not be cohorted solely on influenza status with a client who also has C. difficile.
findings.fix: Keep the qualification in the visible rows, captions and narration: cohort only with the same pathogen and compatible concurrent infection/precaution status, considering roommate risks. Do not leave this condition solely in the facts or SVG description.

findings.where: Images 1, 7, 8 and 14: Transport panel; step transport caption/narration; fact 8
findings.title: Varicella transport teaching omits covering lesions
findings.problem: The transport instruction gives masking as the action and explicitly includes chickenpox, but never teaches covering affected skin lesions. Airborne transport guidance also calls for covering varicella/zoster lesions to reduce contact transmission and dispersal from lesions; a surgical mask does not address that route.
findings.fix: Add the lesion-covering requirement to the transport panel and narration. State that the client wears a surgical mask if tolerated and that affected varicella/zoster lesions are covered during essential transport.

findings.title: The contact animation never makes contact
findings.problem: The glove's lowest point is y + 28, and its maximum downward translation is 8, so it stops at y + 36 while the rail is at y + 46. The supposed transferred germ is drawn six units below the glove rather than on it. The animation therefore does not show the touch-and-carry mechanism it was written to demonstrate.
findings.fix: Adjust the motion so the glove visibly touches the contaminated rail, then lifts away. Position the transferred germ on the glove and synchronize its appearance with the contact phase.

assessment: Hold publication. The condition matcher has reproducible wrong-precaution branches. The visible cohorting and transport instructions also omit relevant safety conditions.
